name: Jong-Hoon Kim
title: Associate Professor
fitReason: Concrete CS-to-physical-AI option spanning video imitation, humanoid motion and interactive robotics. An eight-week project could plausibly focus on evaluation or a bounded pipeline component, but that is a scoping suggestion rather than an advertised placement.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full September 22, 2026 author preprint reports a video-to-motion pipeline using GVHMR, GMR and an existing BeyondMimic/Booster training stack. Its learned policy was deployed via Ethernet on a physical Booster K1: 20 five-meter catwalk trials, approximately 23 steps each, with loose safety belts and no reported falls. The authors are affiliated with the Kent ATR lab, with a Vilnius co-affiliation. This is actual learned policy execution, not only retargeted motion or simulation. It is an integration/application study; it does not establish a new general-purpose foundation model or broad autonomous navigation.

shortVisit.summary: The live ATR roster lists a visiting external master’s student in 2026, but a roster is precedent rather than an invitation. The advertised 2026 summer internship is expressly for high-school students. No current external-master’s short-visit invitation was established; the generic Apply Here destination could not be retrieved.

scoreReasons.fit: 36/40: substantive learned humanoid and interactive-robot integration; narrower application-oriented methods rather than established broad foundation-model development.
scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: current attributable primary paper directly reports real learned humanoid execution.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 0/20: a past/current visitor roster and high-school program do not establish an external-master invitation.
scoreReasons.freshness: 15/15: substantive physical-AI research from September 2026, supported by current official affiliation.

Kent’s current hosting page excludes student positions such as Research Assistant from its Professor/Scholar/Short-Term Scholar documents. The correct appointment for an enrolled external master’s researcher must be resolved with ISSS; this wording is not interpreted as a blanket ban on every externally enrolled student.

The separately published exchange/visiting-student program permits graduate participation case by case but is tuition-bearing coursework-oriented information. It is not proof of a research-only eight-week route.
A 2024 scholar guide lists a $1,400 monthly support threshold, but its currency for 2027 and permitted funding sources for the eventual student appointment remain unverified.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
